When a ClickUp task representing a product requirement is updated, GAIA flags the relevant Linear issues so engineers know what changed without switching tools.

Teams that have tried to consolidate on a single tool and failed because different functions have strong preferences will find this integration especially valuable. GAIA lets each team work in their preferred tool while maintaining a shared source of truth that neither has to maintain manually.

useCases.title: Propagate Linear issue status to ClickUp tasks
useCases.description: When a Linear issue moves to In Review or Done, GAIA updates the linked ClickUp task status so project managers always have a real-time view of engineering progress without pinging engineers for updates.

useCases.title: Create Linear issues from ClickUp requirements tasks
useCases.description: When a product requirement task in ClickUp is approved and ready for development, GAIA creates corresponding Linear issues with priority, description, and due date pre-populated from the ClickUp task.

useCases.title: Sync ClickUp sprint timelines to Linear cycles
useCases.description: GAIA reads ClickUp sprint dates and creates matching Linear cycles, ensuring engineering sprints are aligned with the delivery schedule tracked in ClickUp without manual date entry in both tools.

useCases.title: Alert engineers to ClickUp scope changes
useCases.description: When a ClickUp task that has linked Linear issues is edited — priority changed, deadline shifted, requirements updated — GAIA posts a comment on the Linear issue summarizing what changed so engineers are never surprised.

useCases.title: Roll up engineering metrics into ClickUp dashboards
useCases.description: GAIA periodically syncs Linear cycle metrics — velocity, completion rate, lead time — into custom fields on the corresponding ClickUp project so leadership can track engineering health alongside other project KPIs.

howItWorks.step: Authorize both platforms
howItWorks.description: Connect your Linear workspace and ClickUp workspace to GAIA. During setup, map Linear teams and projects to the corresponding ClickUp Spaces and Lists.

howItWorks.step: Set sync direction and field mappings
howItWorks.description: Define which fields are authoritative in which tool, which status values map between platforms, and which events should trigger cross-platform actions.

howItWorks.step: GAIA handles ongoing synchronization
howItWorks.description: From that point on, GAIA monitors both tools and applies updates automatically. Engineers and project managers each work in their preferred tool with confidence that the other side stays current.

faqs.question: Can GAIA handle the different status models between Linear and ClickUp?
faqs.answer: Yes. During setup you provide a status mapping table — for example, Linear's In Progress maps to ClickUp's In Development, and Linear's Done maps to ClickUp's Completed. GAIA applies this mapping consistently so statuses are always semantically equivalent.

faqs.question: What happens to ClickUp tasks that have no Linear counterpart?
faqs.answer: GAIA only acts on tasks and issues that are explicitly linked or match your configured sync rules. Unlinked ClickUp tasks are untouched. You can trigger issue creation in Linear from ClickUp manually by assigning a specific label or status.

faqs.question: Is there a limit to how many issues GAIA can sync?
faqs.answer: GAIA's sync capacity scales with your plan. Most engineering teams sync hundreds to thousands of issues per month without hitting limits. For very large ClickUp workspaces, you can scope sync to specific Lists or Tags to keep volume manageable.

linear-todoist.tagline: Turn Linear issues assigned to you into personal Todoist tasks automatically
linear-todoist.metaTitle: Linear と Todoist の連携: Linearの課題を個人タスクに
linear-todoist.metaDescription: LinearとTodoistをGAIAで連携。Linearの課題が自分に割り当てられるとTodoistタスクを自動作成し、完了も同期。開発の作業量を個人のタスクと一か所で管理できます。
linear-todoist.intro:
Most engineers manage their work in at least two places: the team issue tracker and their personal task manager. Linear drives the sprint; Todoist (or a notebook, or a whiteboard) drives the individual. Keeping both aligned manually is friction that adds up — copying issue titles, tracking due dates in two places, remembering to mark things done in both systems.

GAIA eliminates that duplication by watching Linear for assignments and automatically creating corresponding tasks in your Todoist. When an issue is assigned to you in Linear, it appears in Todoist with the right project, priority, and due date. When you complete it in either tool, GAIA marks it done in the other. Your personal task list reflects your real engineering workload without any manual copying.

This integration is ideal for engineers who use Todoist as their single place for all tasks — personal errands, recurring work, and engineering tickets — and want Linear to feed into that system automatically rather than competing with it.

useCases.title: Auto-create Todoist tasks from Linear assignments
useCases.description: Every time a Linear issue is assigned to you, GAIA creates a matching Todoist task with the issue title, Linear URL, priority, and target date so your personal task list is always current without any manual entry.

useCases.title: Sync task completion back to Linear
useCases.description: When you check off a task in Todoist, GAIA marks the linked Linear issue as completed so your team's board stays accurate even if you prefer to track your own work in Todoist.

useCases.title: Organize Linear issues by project in Todoist
useCases.description: GAIA maps Linear teams and projects to Todoist projects so engineering work lands in the right section of your task list and doesn't get mixed up with unrelated personal tasks.

useCases.title: Morning digest of today's Linear priorities
useCases.description: Each morning GAIA checks your Linear queue for high-priority issues due today or overdue and adds a Todoist task reminding you to review and action them before daily standup.

useCases.title: Flag overdue Linear issues in Todoist
useCases.description: When a Linear issue's due date passes without resolution, GAIA creates an urgent Todoist task flagging the overdue issue so it surfaces in your personal productivity system and doesn't get buried on the team board.

howItWorks.step: Connect Linear and Todoist to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Linear account and your Todoist account. GAIA identifies which Linear user you are and maps your assignments to your Todoist inbox.

howItWorks.step: Configure project mapping and sync preferences
howItWorks.description: Choose which Linear teams or projects should feed into Todoist, which Todoist project each should map to, and whether completions should sync bidirectionally.

howItWorks.step: Work across both tools seamlessly
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors your Linear assignments and keeps your Todoist updated automatically. You can triage your day in Todoist while teammates see accurate status in Linear.

faqs.question: Will GAIA create a Todoist task for every Linear issue in the workspace or only my assignments?
faqs.answer: By default GAIA only creates Todoist tasks for issues assigned to your Linear user. You can optionally configure it to also watch issues you've subscribed to or issues in a specific team regardless of assignment.

faqs.question: What happens when a Linear issue is reassigned away from me?
faqs.answer: GAIA detects the reassignment and marks the corresponding Todoist task as cancelled or deletes it, depending on your preference. This prevents stale tasks from cluttering your personal list.

faqs.question: Can I edit the Todoist task without affecting Linear?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can freely edit the Todoist task title, add subtasks, set reminders, or move it to a different project without those changes touching Linear. Only task completion is synced back; everything else is yours to manage locally.

linear-trello.tagline: Link Trello product roadmap cards to Linear engineering issues seamlessly
linear-trello.metaTitle: Linear と Trello の連携: ロードマップと開発課題をつなぐ
linear-trello.metaDescription: LinearとTrelloをGAIAで連携。TrelloのロードマップカードをLinearの開発課題に自動で紐付け、ステータスの更新を伝播。手動の同期なしでプロダクトと開発を揃えます。
linear-trello.intro:
Product teams that plan roadmaps in Trello and engineering teams that execute in Linear often struggle to keep both views in sync. A Trello card representing a roadmap feature may spawn ten Linear issues, but the Trello card has no idea when those issues are completed. Product managers watch the Trello board and have no signal that engineering has shipped the underlying work.

GAIA creates and maintains the link between Trello cards and Linear issues so product and engineering always share the same reality. When a Trello card moves to In Development, GAIA creates the corresponding Linear issues. As those issues progress and complete, GAIA updates the Trello card automatically. When the last issue ships, the Trello card moves to Done.

This integration suits companies that want to keep using Trello for high-level roadmap planning — its visual simplicity and broad accessibility make it popular with non-technical stakeholders — while giving engineering the power of Linear for day-to-day sprint work.

useCases.title: Create Linear issues from Trello cards
useCases.description: When a Trello card is moved to the Ready for Development list, GAIA breaks it into Linear issues based on the card checklist items, assigns them to the relevant Linear team, and attaches the Trello card URL for reference.

useCases.title: Update Trello card status from Linear progress
useCases.description: As Linear issues linked to a Trello card progress, GAIA updates the card's checklist items and custom fields so product managers see a live progress indicator on the roadmap card without checking Linear.

useCases.title: Auto-move Trello cards when all issues ship
useCases.description: When all Linear issues linked to a Trello card are marked Done, GAIA automatically moves the card to the Shipped list on the Trello board, giving the roadmap an accurate picture of what has been delivered.

useCases.title: Attach Linear cycle info to Trello cards
useCases.description: GAIA writes the target Linear cycle to a Trello card's label or custom field so product managers can see at a glance which sprint a feature is scheduled for without asking engineering.

useCases.title: Notify Trello card members of Linear blockers
useCases.description: When a Linear issue linked to a Trello card moves to Blocked, GAIA adds a comment to the Trello card summarizing the blocker so product owners can take cross-team action without waiting for standup.

howItWorks.step: Connect Trello and Linear to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Trello account and Linear workspace. Map Trello boards to Linear teams and define which Trello lists correspond to which development stages.

howItWorks.step: Define creation and sync triggers
howItWorks.description: Specify which Trello list moves trigger Linear issue creation, how Trello checklist items map to Linear issue titles, and which Linear state changes should update the Trello card.

howItWorks.step: Keep roadmap and sprint board aligned automatically
howItWorks.description: GAIA handles all cross-tool updates from that point. Product managers work in Trello, engineers work in Linear, and both boards stay synchronized without anyone manually managing the connection.

faqs.question: Can one Trello card be linked to multiple Linear issues?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is the typical use case. A single Trello roadmap card often represents a feature that requires multiple engineering tasks. GAIA tracks all linked Linear issues and rolls up their status to the Trello card automatically.

faqs.question: Does GAIA work with Trello Power-Ups?
faqs.answer: GAIA operates through the Trello API and works alongside existing Power-Ups without conflict. It uses standard Trello card fields, custom fields, and comments, so it is compatible with most popular Trello Power-Up configurations.

faqs.question: What if we move a Trello card back to a previous list?
faqs.answer: GAIA detects backward movement and can optionally reopen the corresponding Linear issues or add a comment to notify the engineering team. You configure whether regressions should trigger automatic actions or just log a notification.

linear-figma.tagline: デザインのプレビューはLinearのFigma連携で、受け渡しまわりのLinear・GitHub・Slackの作業はGAIAで
linear-figma.metaTitle: Linear と Figma の連携: デザインを課題に添付
linear-figma.metaDescription: LinearのFigma連携は課題内にデザインをプレビューし、Figmaプラグインはフレームから課題を作成します。GAIAはLinear、GitHub、Slack側の作業を担います。
linear-figma.intro:
FigmaをLinearと連携するには、Linearの連携設定からLinear公式のFigma連携を有効にします。以降は、FigmaのファイルやフレームのリンクをLinearの課題やコメントに貼ると、デザインのライブプレビューが表示されます。Figma側では、LinearのFigmaプラグインを使えば、ファイルを離れずに選択したフレームからLinearの課題を作成したり、既存の課題を紐づけたりできます。この2つがLinearとFigmaの公式連携です。デザインを課題に添付し、デザインから課題を作る、という役割です。

チームでGitHubとSlackも使っているなら、それらもLinearでネイティブに接続しましょう。GitHub連携はプルリクエストを課題に紐づけ、プルリクエストのオープンやマージに合わせて課題を進めます。Slack連携はメッセージから課題を作成し、課題の更新をチャンネルに投稿します。3つとも有効にすれば、Linear、GitHub、Figma、Slackの間で、別のツールを挟まずにリンクとプレビューが共有されます。

GAIAはFigmaに接続しないため、ファイル内のフレーム、バージョン、コメントは読めません。GAIAが担うのは、Linear、GitHub、Slackでのデザイン受け渡しまわりの作業です。渡されたFigmaリンク付きでLinearの課題を作成し、課題の作成・更新・コメントに反応し、対応が必要なときはSlackでデザイナーやエンジニアに知らせます。GAIAではLinearのイベントトリガーが使えるので、こうしたワークフローはスケジュールだけでなく、課題が変わった時点で実行できます。

useCases.title: デザインリンク付きでLinearの課題を作成
useCases.description: チャットにFigmaリンクを貼って作業内容を説明すると、GAIAが適切なチームにタイトル、説明、FigmaのURL付きでLinearの課題を作成します。LinearのFigma連携がプレビューを表示します。

useCases.title: デザインレビューのメモをLinearの課題に変換
useCases.description: レビューのメモや修正依頼の一覧を貼ると、GAIAが項目ごとに対応するFigmaリンク付きのLinear課題を作成し、指定した担当者、ラベル、サイクルも設定します。

useCases.title: 実装開始をデザイナーに知らせる
useCases.description: Linearの課題更新をトリガーにしたワークフローが、designラベルの付いた課題がIn Progressに移ったことを検知し、課題のリンクを添えてSlackでデザイナーに知らせます。

useCases.title: デザイン課題への技術的な質問をSlackに流す
useCases.description: designラベルの付いたLinear課題にコメントが付くと、GAIAがコメントと課題のリンクをSlackのデザインチャンネルに投稿します。デザイナーはLinearを見張らなくても質問に気づけます。

useCases.title: デザイン受け渡しの週次レポートを送る
useCases.description: 毎週GAIAがLinearでデザイン関連の課題を検索し、デザイン待ちのもの、開発中のもの、説明にFigmaリンクがない課題をまとめて送ります。

howItWorks.step: LinearのFigma連携を有効にし、LinearをGAIAに接続
howItWorks.description: プレビューのためにLinearでFigma連携を有効にし、デザイナーがFigmaから課題を作りたい場合はFigmaにLinearプラグインをインストールします。そのうえで連携ページからLinearをGAIAに接続し、ワークフローで使うならSlackやGitHubも接続します。

howItWorks.step: ワークフローを自然な言葉で説明
howItWorks.description: たとえば「designラベルの付いたLinear課題がIn Progressになったら、Slackの#designで担当デザイナーに知らせて」というワークフローを作成します。チャットでFigmaリンクから課題を作るよう頼むこともできます。

howItWorks.step: GAIAがバックグラウンドで実行
howItWorks.description: トリガー型のワークフローはLinearのイベントが届いた時点で、スケジュール型は設定した時刻に実行され、それぞれ実行内容を報告します。課題やコメントの削除などの破壊的な操作は、承認設定に従います。

faqs.question: GAIAはFigmaのフレームとLinearの課題をどうやって自動で対応付けますか？
faqs.answer: 対応付けません。GAIAはFigmaに接続しないため、Figmaファイルを検索したり、名前でフレームを対応付けたりはできません。リンクはあなたやチームが用意します。課題にFigmaのURLを貼るか（GAIAが代わりに課題を作るときはURLを入れます）、LinearのプラグインでFigmaから課題を作成してください。

faqs.question: GAIAはLinearにFigmaのプレビューを直接埋め込めますか？
faqs.answer: プレビューを表示するのはGAIAではなく、LinearのFigma連携です。有効にすれば、課題の説明やコメント内のFigmaリンクはすべてプレビュー表示されます。GAIAが課題の作成・更新時に追加したリンクも同様です。

faqs.question: GAIAはデザインのバージョン管理のためのFigmaブランチに対応していますか？
faqs.answer: 対応していません。GAIAはFigmaのブランチ、バージョン、マージを見られません。デザインの確定をLinearに反映したい場合は、デザイナーに課題のステータス変更やラベル追加をしてもらえば、GAIAのワークフローがLinear上のその変更に反応できます。

faqs.question: FigmaとLinearを連携するにはどうすればよいですか？
faqs.answer: Linearの連携設定からFigma連携を有効にし、Figmaアカウントでサインインします。課題にFigmaリンクを貼ればプレビューが表示されます。デザイナーはFigmaにLinearプラグインをインストールして、フレームから課題を作成・紐づけすることもできます。

faqs.question: Linear、GitHub、Figma、Slackをつなぐにはどうすればよいですか？
faqs.answer: それぞれLinearのネイティブ連携を使います。デザインのプレビューにはFigma、プルリクエストの紐づけと課題ステータスの更新にはGitHub、メッセージからの課題作成と更新の投稿にはSlackです。ツールをまたいだ定型作業がほしいときにGAIAを加えましょう。課題が開発に入ったらSlackでデザイナーに知らせる、週次で受け渡し状況をまとめる、といった使い方です。

faqs.question: LinearとFigmaの公式連携はありますか？
faqs.answer: あります。LinearはFigma連携とFigmaプラグインを自社で提供しています。GAIAはどちらの代わりにもならず、受け渡しのうちLinear、GitHub、Slack側を担います。

linear-discord.tagline: Post Linear issue updates to dev Discord channels automatically
linear-discord.metaTitle: Linear Discord 連携: 課題の通知をサーバーへ
linear-discord.metaDescription: Linearの担当割り当てをDMで、優先度の高い課題やブロッカーを適切なチャンネルへ通知し、スプリント完了も共有。GAIAが通知を絞ります。設定手順をご覧ください。
linear-discord.intro:
Engineering teams that use Discord as their primary communication platform often miss Linear updates because important context stays siloed in the issue tracker. An issue moving to Blocked has no way to interrupt the Discord conversation. A sprint completing with a great velocity goes unannounced. New issues assigned to engineers sit unread while the team chats in Discord.

GAIA brings Linear into Discord by routing the right events to the right channels automatically. High-priority issues get announced in the engineering channel. Blockers alert the relevant team leads. Sprint completions trigger automated summaries. Engineers can even create and update Linear issues directly from Discord commands without switching tools.

This integration is particularly valuable for remote-first engineering teams that treat Discord as their virtual office and want Linear activity to surface there naturally rather than requiring constant tab-switching.

useCases.title: Post issue assignments to personal Discord DMs
useCases.description: When a Linear issue is assigned to an engineer, GAIA sends them a Discord DM with the issue title, priority, description, and a direct link so they are notified immediately in the tool they are already using.

useCases.title: Announce sprint completions to the engineering channel
useCases.description: When a Linear cycle ends, GAIA posts a formatted sprint summary to the designated Discord channel showing issues completed, carry-over, team velocity, and top contributors to celebrate the team's work.

useCases.title: Alert the team to new high-priority issues
useCases.description: When a Linear issue is created or upgraded to Urgent priority, GAIA immediately posts an alert to the engineering Discord channel with full context so the team can react and assign it without delay.

useCases.title: Post blocker alerts to the leads channel
useCases.description: When a Linear issue transitions to Blocked, GAIA sends a structured alert to the team leads Discord channel including the blocking dependency, the affected engineer, and the issue's current due date so blockers are resolved quickly.

useCases.title: Create Linear issues from Discord commands
useCases.description: Engineers can type a GAIA command in Discord to create a new Linear issue without leaving the chat. GAIA prompts for title, priority, and assignee, creates the issue, and posts the confirmation link back to the channel.

howItWorks.step: Connect Linear and Discord to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Linear workspace and invite the GAIA bot to your Discord server. Map Linear teams to Discord channels during setup.

howItWorks.step: Configure notification rules and channel routing
howItWorks.description: Choose which Linear events generate Discord notifications, which channels should receive which event types, and the format of notification messages.

howItWorks.step: Linear activity flows into Discord automatically
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors Linear for the configured events and posts formatted updates to the right Discord channels in real time. The team stays informed without leaving Discord.

faqs.question: Can GAIA send Linear notifications to different Discord channels based on the team or project?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can configure channel routing rules so that Linear Team A notifications go to #team-alpha and Team B notifications go to #team-beta. You can also route by event type, priority, or label.

faqs.question: Can engineers interact with Linear issues directly from Discord?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA supports Discord slash commands for common Linear actions including creating issues, updating status, adding comments, and querying the current sprint state. Responses are posted in-thread so the channel stays clean.

faqs.question: How does GAIA handle Discord notification fatigue?
faqs.answer: You control the event filters. Most teams configure GAIA to notify only on priority thresholds (e.g., Urgent and High only), specific labels, or specific issue state transitions rather than every Linear event. This keeps Discord signal-to-noise high.

linear-drive.tagline: Attach design docs and specs from Google Drive to Linear issues automatically
linear-drive.metaTitle: Linear と Google Drive の連携: ドキュメントを課題に添付
linear-drive.metaDescription: LinearとGoogle DriveをGAIAで連携。関連するDriveのドキュメントをLinearの課題に自動添付し、課題の説明から仕様書を作成。開発ドキュメントを作業と結び付けて管理できます。
linear-drive.intro:
Engineering issues rarely exist in isolation. Behind most Linear issues is a Google Drive folder full of context: the product spec, the design doc, the API contract, the meeting notes from the scoping session. But that context lives in Drive while the issue lives in Linear, and the link between them is usually an afterthought — a URL pasted into a comment that gets buried, or nothing at all.

GAIA builds and maintains the connection between Drive documents and Linear issues automatically. When a new feature issue is created in Linear, GAIA searches the configured Drive folder for matching spec documents and attaches them. When a new spec doc is created in Drive and follows your team's naming convention, GAIA creates the corresponding Linear issue and links back to the doc.

This integration eliminates the document hunt that slows down engineers at the start of every task and ensures that the historical context behind an issue is always one click away.

useCases.title: Auto-attach Drive spec docs to Linear issues
useCases.description: When a new Linear issue is created with the feature label, GAIA searches the product specs folder in Drive for a document matching the issue title and attaches the link automatically so engineers have immediate access to the specification.

useCases.title: Create Linear issues from new Drive spec docs
useCases.description: When a new spec document is added to the designated Drive folder and marked Ready for Engineering, GAIA creates a corresponding Linear issue with the document title, a description pulled from the doc summary, and a link back to Drive.

useCases.title: Attach meeting notes to related Linear issues
useCases.description: When a Google Doc meeting note is created after an engineering planning session and contains Linear issue IDs in the title or body, GAIA attaches the note to each referenced issue so decision context is preserved.

useCases.title: Generate post-mortem docs in Drive from Linear incidents
useCases.description: When a Linear issue labeled incident is resolved, GAIA creates a post-mortem document in the designated Drive folder pre-populated with the issue title, timeline, and description so the team can fill in the analysis without starting from scratch.

useCases.title: Organize Drive docs by Linear project
useCases.description: GAIA maintains a Drive folder structure mirroring your Linear projects. When an issue is created in a Linear project, GAIA creates a corresponding subfolder in Drive so all related documents are organized consistently without manual folder management.

howItWorks.step: Connect Google Drive and Linear to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Google Workspace account and Linear workspace. Designate the Drive folders GAIA should watch and search, and map them to Linear teams or projects.

howItWorks.step: Configure matching rules and triggers
howItWorks.description: Define the naming conventions GAIA should use to match Drive documents to Linear issues, which Drive events should create Linear issues, and which Linear events should create Drive documents.

howItWorks.step: Documentation attaches to issues automatically
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors both platforms and maintains the links between issues and documents in real time. Engineers find their specs in Linear; documents in Drive always reference their related issues.

faqs.question: Does GAIA require a specific naming convention for Drive documents?
faqs.answer: GAIA works best with consistent naming conventions but can also be configured with flexible matching patterns using regular expressions. You can also link Drive documents to Linear issues manually and GAIA will register and maintain those explicit links.

faqs.question: Can GAIA attach shared Drive files or only files owned by me?
faqs.answer: GAIA can attach any Drive file that the authorized Google account has access to, including shared drives and files shared with your domain. It respects existing Drive sharing permissions and does not change access settings.

faqs.question: What file types does GAIA support when attaching Drive files to Linear?
faqs.answer: GAIA can attach links to any Drive file type including Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, and uploaded PDFs, images, or other files. Linear renders the attached URLs with metadata previews for Google Workspace file types.

linear-hubspot.tagline: Link customer feature requests from HubSpot to Linear engineering issues
linear-hubspot.metaTitle: Linear + HubSpot Integration - Customer Requests Drive Engineering
linear-hubspot.metaDescription: Connect Linear and HubSpot with GAIA. Automatically create Linear issues from HubSpot customer feature requests, link deals to issues, and notify sales when engineering ships customer-requested features.
linear-hubspot.intro:
Customer-facing teams log feature requests and bug reports in HubSpot every day. Engineering tracks their work in Linear. But the path from a HubSpot contact's request to a Linear issue on the sprint board is almost always a manual one — someone reads CRM notes, decides it is worth building, creates a Linear issue, and then forgets to update HubSpot when the feature ships.

GAIA closes the loop between customer feedback and engineering delivery. When a HubSpot deal or ticket contains a feature request that meets your threshold for engineering consideration, GAIA creates the Linear issue with full customer context attached. When engineering ships the feature in Linear, GAIA updates HubSpot and notifies the account owner so they can follow up with the customer.

This integration is most impactful for B2B SaaS teams where engineering prioritization is influenced by customer revenue potential and where sales and customer success teams need visibility into when requested features ship.

useCases.title: Create Linear issues from HubSpot feature request tickets
useCases.description: When a HubSpot support ticket is tagged as Feature Request and meets your minimum deal-value threshold, GAIA creates a Linear issue with the customer context, associated deal value, and HubSpot ticket link so engineering has all the information needed to evaluate and prioritize.

useCases.title: Notify account owners when features ship
useCases.description: When a Linear issue linked to a HubSpot deal is marked Done, GAIA creates a HubSpot activity on the deal notifying the account owner that the requested feature has shipped, giving them a timely reason to reach out to the customer.

useCases.title: Aggregate customer demand to prioritize Linear backlog
useCases.description: GAIA counts how many HubSpot contacts have requested a given feature and writes that demand count to the corresponding Linear issue's metadata. Product teams can sort the Linear backlog by customer demand to inform sprint prioritization.

useCases.title: Link HubSpot bug reports to existing Linear issues
useCases.description: When a customer reports a bug in HubSpot that matches an already-open Linear issue by keyword or description similarity, GAIA links the HubSpot ticket to the existing issue and increments an affected-customers counter rather than creating duplicates.

useCases.title: Update HubSpot deal stage when engineering milestones are hit
useCases.description: When a Linear project associated with a HubSpot opportunity reaches a configurable completion percentage, GAIA moves the deal to the relevant pipeline stage — such as Feature In Beta — so sales stays in sync with engineering progress.

howItWorks.step: Connect HubSpot and Linear to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your HubSpot portal and Linear workspace. Define which HubSpot deal stages, ticket types, or properties should trigger Linear issue creation.

howItWorks.step: Configure customer context mapping
howItWorks.description: Map HubSpot deal properties — company name, ARR, contact owner — to Linear issue fields or labels so engineering always sees the business context behind a feature request.

howItWorks.step: Close the loop between customers and engineering
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors both platforms and propagates updates in both directions. Sales knows when features ship. Engineering knows how much customer demand backs each backlog item.

faqs.question: Can GAIA filter which HubSpot tickets create Linear issues based on deal value?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can set a minimum associated deal value threshold so only feature requests from accounts above a certain ARR generate Linear issues automatically. Requests below the threshold are logged in GAIA's queue for manual review.

faqs.question: How does GAIA avoid creating duplicate Linear issues when multiple customers report the same request?
faqs.answer: GAIA uses semantic similarity matching to identify Linear issues that likely correspond to an incoming HubSpot request. If a match above your configured confidence threshold exists, GAIA links the HubSpot ticket to the existing issue and increments the demand count rather than creating a duplicate.

faqs.question: Does GAIA sync back to HubSpot when a Linear issue is partially complete, or only when Done?
faqs.answer: You can configure sync triggers for any Linear state transition. Common configurations notify HubSpot at In Review (feature in beta) and Done (feature shipped), giving account owners two touchpoints to manage customer expectations.

linear-zoom.tagline: Schedule sprint ceremonies and post Zoom summaries to Linear issues automatically
linear-zoom.metaTitle: Linear と Zoom の連携: スプリント会議と課題管理
linear-zoom.metaDescription: LinearとZoomをGAIAで連携。Linearのサイクルの日程からスプリントの会議を自動設定し、Zoomの要約を課題に投稿。アクションアイテムは新しい課題として記録できます。
linear-zoom.intro:
Engineering sprint ceremonies — planning, standup, review, retrospective — happen in Zoom. The action items, decisions, and issue updates from those meetings should live in Linear. But capturing that context from a Zoom call and getting it back into Linear requires someone to take notes, identify action items, and manually create or update Linear issues after every meeting. That process is rarely done consistently.

GAIA automates the connection between Zoom meetings and Linear by scheduling ceremonies automatically from cycle dates, transcribing and summarizing meetings, and extracting action items as new Linear issues. The team gets a meeting record attached to the right sprint without anyone spending time on post-meeting admin.

This integration is ideal for remote engineering teams that run all their ceremonies over Zoom and want the insights from those meetings captured in Linear automatically rather than lost in meeting notes that nobody reads.

useCases.title: Auto-schedule sprint ceremonies from Linear cycles
useCases.description: When a new Linear cycle is created, GAIA schedules recurring Zoom meetings for sprint planning, daily standup, sprint review, and retrospective based on the cycle dates and the team's configured ceremony cadence.

useCases.title: Post Zoom meeting summaries to Linear cycles
useCases.description: After a sprint ceremony ends on Zoom, GAIA generates a meeting summary using the transcript and attaches it as a comment on the corresponding Linear cycle so the team has a searchable record of what was discussed.

useCases.title: Create Linear issues from Zoom action items
useCases.description: GAIA identifies action items in Zoom meeting transcripts — commitments, follow-up tasks, blockers raised — and creates corresponding Linear issues assigned to the relevant team member with the meeting context as the issue description.

useCases.title: Add Zoom recording links to Linear issues
useCases.description: After a Zoom call that references specific Linear issues by ID, GAIA attaches the Zoom recording link to each mentioned issue so engineers can review the conversation context without asking for the recording link.

useCases.title: Generate sprint review agenda from Linear cycle
useCases.description: Before the sprint review Zoom meeting, GAIA generates an agenda document listing all completed Linear issues with their titles and descriptions, ready to share as a Zoom meeting document so the team can walk through shipped work systematically.

howItWorks.step: Connect Zoom and Linear to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Zoom account and Linear workspace. Configure the ceremony types, their default durations, and the Zoom meeting settings GAIA should use when scheduling.

howItWorks.step: Map ceremony types to Linear events
howItWorks.description: Tell GAIA which Linear cycle events should trigger which Zoom meeting types and where meeting summaries and action items should be posted in Linear.

howItWorks.step: Sprint ceremonies schedule and document themselves
howItWorks.description: GAIA creates Zoom meetings when cycles start, joins the meetings to capture transcripts, and posts summaries and action items to Linear automatically after each ceremony ends.

faqs.question: Does GAIA join Zoom meetings automatically or only if invited?
faqs.answer: GAIA joins meetings it schedules automatically. For meetings you schedule independently, you can invite GAIA's Zoom participant link and it will join, transcribe, and post a summary to your configured Linear destination.

faqs.question: How accurate is GAIA's action item extraction from Zoom transcripts?
faqs.answer: GAIA uses structured prompt analysis on Zoom transcripts to identify action items with high confidence. It flags extracted items for human review before creating Linear issues, so you can approve, edit, or discard each one before it enters the backlog.

faqs.question: Can GAIA schedule Zoom meetings based on team members' calendar availability?
faqs.answer: Yes. When connected to Google Calendar or Outlook, GAIA checks team member availability before scheduling ceremony times and picks the slot with the best attendance overlap within your configured working hours.

linear-airtable.tagline: Sync engineering metrics and issue data to Airtable dashboards
linear-airtable.metaTitle: Linear と Airtable の連携: 開発指標をAirtableに集約
linear-airtable.metaDescription: LinearとAirtableをGAIAで連携。Linearの課題とスプリント指標をAirtableに自動同期し、開発ダッシュボードを構築。非技術職の関係者も開発の成果を把握できます。
linear-airtable.intro:
Linear is purpose-built for engineering teams. Airtable is purpose-built for structured data that non-technical stakeholders can query, filter, and build views on. The two serve different audiences, but the data that lives in Linear — issue counts, cycle velocity, lead times, label breakdowns — is exactly what operations, finance, and product leadership want to analyze in Airtable.

GAIA syncs Linear data to Airtable automatically so dashboards stay current without anyone manually exporting CSVs. Engineering metrics flow into Airtable bases where stakeholders can build the views, formulas, and reports they need without accessing Linear. When an issue is created, updated, or completed in Linear, Airtable reflects the change in real time.

This integration is particularly useful for ops teams that track engineering KPIs alongside other business metrics in Airtable, and for companies that use Airtable as their source of truth for cross-functional reporting.

useCases.title: Mirror Linear issues to an Airtable issues base
useCases.description: GAIA creates a row in Airtable for each Linear issue in your configured scope, keeping fields like status, assignee, priority, label, and cycle synchronized so stakeholders can query, filter, and group issues without Linear access.

useCases.title: Sync cycle metrics to an engineering KPIs base
useCases.description: At the end of each Linear cycle, GAIA appends a new record to the engineering KPIs Airtable base with velocity, completion rate, carry-over percentage, and average cycle time so leadership can track engineering health over time.

useCases.title: Build bug triage views in Airtable
useCases.description: GAIA syncs all Linear issues labeled bug to a dedicated Airtable base where the support team can add triage notes, customer impact ratings, and reproduction steps that live alongside the engineering issue data without cluttering Linear.

useCases.title: Track feature delivery commitments in Airtable
useCases.description: GAIA syncs Linear issues linked to committed features to an Airtable tracking base. Stakeholders see target cycle, current status, and actual delivery date in a format they can embed in executive reports.

useCases.title: Aggregate team capacity data for resource planning
useCases.description: GAIA writes assigned issue counts, story points, and cycle allocations per engineer to an Airtable resource planning base so ops and engineering management can model capacity without manual data collection.

howItWorks.step: Connect Linear and Airtable to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Linear workspace and Airtable account. Select or create the Airtable base and tables that should receive Linear data.

howItWorks.step: Map Linear fields to Airtable columns
howItWorks.description: Define which Linear issue properties map to which Airtable columns. GAIA supports all standard Linear fields as well as custom fields and will create Airtable columns for any that do not already exist.

howItWorks.step: Airtable stays current as Linear changes
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors Linear for issue changes and propagates them to Airtable in near real time. Stakeholders always see current data in their Airtable views without anyone running exports.

faqs.question: Does GAIA sync historical Linear issues or only new activity?
faqs.answer: On initial setup, GAIA performs a historical backfill of all existing Linear issues within your configured scope. Going forward, new issues and updates sync in near real time.

faqs.question: Can Airtable team members update rows and have those changes reflected back in Linear?
faqs.answer: Bidirectional sync is supported for a limited set of fields — primarily status and assignee. For most teams, Linear is treated as the authoritative source and Airtable is read-optimized, but you can enable write-back for specific columns during setup.

faqs.question: How does GAIA handle Linear issues that are deleted?
faqs.answer: When a Linear issue is deleted, GAIA marks the corresponding Airtable row as archived rather than deleting it, so your historical reporting data is preserved. You can configure hard deletion if your data retention policy requires it.

linear-stripe.tagline: Link payment bugs to Linear and prioritize issues by revenue impact
linear-stripe.metaTitle: Linear と Stripe の連携: 売上を意識した開発の優先順位
linear-stripe.metaDescription: LinearとStripeをGAIAで連携。Stripeの支払い失敗からLinearの課題を自動作成し、バグに売上の背景情報を添付。顧客への影響が大きい開発課題を優先できます。
linear-stripe.intro:
Payment failures and billing edge cases discovered in Stripe often lack a clear path to the engineering team. A spike in failed charges that surfaces in the Stripe dashboard requires someone to notice it, decide it is an engineering problem, find the right Linear team, and create an issue with enough context to act on. That chain of manual steps means payment issues sit unresolved longer than they should.

GAIA connects Stripe to Linear so payment-related engineering issues are created automatically with full financial context. When Stripe detects a spike in payment failures, a webhook error, or a subscription lifecycle issue, GAIA creates a Linear issue with the Stripe event data, affected customer count, and estimated revenue impact so engineers can prioritize it accurately.

This integration is most valuable for SaaS companies where payment reliability is directly tied to revenue and where engineering prioritization should reflect the business impact of technical issues.

useCases.title: Create Linear issues from Stripe payment failure spikes
useCases.description: When Stripe's failure rate for a given payment method or error code exceeds a configurable threshold, GAIA creates a high-priority Linear issue with the error breakdown, affected customer count, and estimated revenue at risk.

useCases.title: Link Stripe webhook failures to Linear bugs
useCases.description: When Stripe reports repeated webhook delivery failures to your endpoint, GAIA creates a Linear bug with the failing event types, response codes, and a timeline of failures so engineering can diagnose and resolve the integration issue quickly.

useCases.title: Attach revenue impact to existing Linear payment issues
useCases.description: For Linear issues already tagged with a payment label, GAIA queries Stripe for related error events and attaches an estimated revenue impact figure derived from the affected customers' MRR so product teams can prioritize by business value.

useCases.title: Alert engineering when Stripe disputes spike
useCases.description: When Stripe dispute volume exceeds a weekly threshold, GAIA creates a Linear investigation issue with a breakdown of the dispute reasons and amounts so the engineering team can identify whether a code change caused the increase.

useCases.title: Close Linear issues when Stripe errors resolve
useCases.description: When a payment error pattern that triggered a Linear issue returns to baseline in Stripe, GAIA adds a resolution comment to the Linear issue and moves it to Done automatically so resolved payment issues do not linger in the backlog.

howItWorks.step: Connect Stripe and Linear to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Stripe account and Linear workspace. Configure the Stripe event types and error thresholds that should trigger Linear issue creation.

howItWorks.step: Set revenue impact thresholds and routing rules
howItWorks.description: Define the minimum failure rate or revenue impact that warrants a Linear issue, which Linear team should receive payment issues, and how Stripe customer data should be summarized in issue descriptions.

howItWorks.step: Payment issues surface in Linear with business context
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors Stripe events and creates Linear issues automatically when thresholds are crossed. Engineers see the financial impact of payment bugs in their issue tracker and can prioritize accordingly.

faqs.question: Does GAIA include customer PII from Stripe in Linear issues?
faqs.answer: No. GAIA is configured to exclude personally identifiable information by default. Linear issues receive aggregate statistics — affected customer count, total revenue at risk, error code distribution — without individual customer names, emails, or payment details.

faqs.question: Can GAIA distinguish between transient Stripe errors and persistent bugs?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA applies a configurable time-window filter so single transient errors do not create Linear issues. A Linear issue is created only when error rates persist above your threshold across a defined window — for example, a 5% failure rate sustained for 10 minutes.

faqs.question: What Stripe events does GAIA monitor beyond payment failures?
faqs.answer: GAIA can monitor any Stripe webhook event including subscription lifecycle events, dispute creation, payout failures, and refund spikes. You configure which event types are relevant for your engineering team during setup.

jira-notion.tagline: Sync Jira epics to Notion project pages and document sprint retros automatically
jira-notion.metaTitle: Jira と Notion の連携: 課題管理とドキュメントをつなぐ
jira-notion.metaDescription: JiraとNotionをGAIAで連携。JiraのエピックをNotionのプロジェクトページに自動同期し、スプリントの振り返りテンプレートを入力。開発文書を進行中のJiraの作業に紐付けます。
jira-notion.intro:
Jira and Notion serve different but complementary roles in a product engineering organization. Jira tracks the executable: stories, bugs, sprints, and releases. Notion holds the interpretive: specs, ADRs, retros, and project narratives. The problem is that the two rarely stay in sync. Sprint retro templates sit empty in Notion while the data exists in Jira. Epic docs in Notion go stale while the actual work evolves in Jira.

GAIA keeps Jira and Notion synchronized without requiring anyone to manually copy data between them. When a Jira epic is created, GAIA scaffolds a Notion project page with the epic context. When a sprint ends, GAIA populates the Notion retro template with data pulled from Jira. When an epic is marked complete in Jira, the Notion page reflects the final state.

This integration is most impactful for product engineering teams that invest in documentation quality and want Notion to always reflect what is actually happening in Jira rather than representing a snapshot from the last time someone remembered to update it.

useCases.title: Scaffold Notion project pages from Jira epics
useCases.description: When a new Jira epic is created, GAIA creates a corresponding Notion project page pre-populated with the epic name, description, acceptance criteria, and a linked table of child stories so the team has a documentation home for the feature from day one.

useCases.title: Auto-populate sprint retrospective templates
useCases.description: At the end of each Jira sprint, GAIA fills the team's Notion retro template with sprint metrics — stories completed, velocity, carry-over, and bugs closed — so the retrospective meeting can focus on insights rather than data gathering.

useCases.title: Embed live Jira story status in Notion specs
useCases.description: GAIA maintains a synchronized table in each Notion epic page showing the current status of all linked Jira stories. Product managers and designers can see engineering progress directly in the spec document without accessing Jira.

useCases.title: Create Jira epics from Notion product briefs
useCases.description: When a Notion product brief is tagged Ready for Engineering, GAIA creates a Jira epic and its child stories from the brief's requirements section, linking each Jira item back to the Notion source document.

useCases.title: Update Notion release notes when Jira versions ship
useCases.description: When a Jira version or release is marked as released, GAIA appends the included stories and bug fixes to the team's Notion release notes page in a formatted, user-facing changelog entry.

howItWorks.step: Connect Jira and Notion to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Jira project and Notion workspace. Map Jira projects to Notion databases or page hierarchies during setup.

howItWorks.step: Configure sync rules and template mappings
howItWorks.description: Specify which Jira events trigger Notion page creation or updates, which Notion page templates should be used for epics and retros, and how Jira fields should map to Notion page properties.

howItWorks.step: Documentation and issues stay synchronized
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors both tools and applies updates automatically. Notion pages reflect the current state of Jira work, and Jira epics can be seeded from Notion product briefs.

faqs.question: Can GAIA sync Jira subtasks to Notion or only epics and stories?
faqs.answer: GAIA supports configurable depth. You can sync only epics, epics and stories, or the full epic-story-subtask hierarchy to Notion. Most teams sync epics and stories to keep Notion at a strategic level while leaving tactical subtask details in Jira.

faqs.question: Will GAIA overwrite content I write manually in a Notion page?
faqs.answer: GAIA writes only to dedicated sections and database properties it manages. Free-form content you add to a Notion page is never modified. GAIA uses clearly marked blocks and properties to separate its automated content from your manual additions.

faqs.question: Does GAIA support Jira Service Management projects as well as Software projects?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA supports both Jira Software and Jira Service Management. For service management projects, GAIA can sync incident and request data to Notion knowledge base pages and post-mortem templates.

jira-todoist.tagline: Create personal Todoist tasks from Jira issues and sync completions back
jira-todoist.metaTitle: Todoist Jira 連携: 担当課題をタスクに
jira-todoist.metaDescription: 担当課題を個人のタスクリストに。GAIAがJiraの課題をTodoistタスクにし、完了するとJiraに反映します。設定手順をご覧ください。
jira-todoist.intro:
Engineers who use Todoist as their personal task hub face a daily friction: Jira is where assignments live, Todoist is where they plan their day, and keeping both aligned requires constant manual effort. An issue assigned in Jira needs to be manually added to Todoist. A task completed in Todoist needs to be manually marked done in Jira. Over time, the two fall out of sync and engineers either abandon Todoist or lose trust in Jira.

GAIA eliminates this friction by bridging Jira and Todoist automatically. When a Jira issue is assigned to you, GAIA creates the corresponding Todoist task with the right project, priority, and due date. When you complete it in Todoist, GAIA transitions the Jira issue to Done. You manage your day in Todoist and your team sees accurate status in Jira.

This integration is ideal for engineers who value a personal task management system that gives them a unified view of all their work — code reviews, meetings, errands, and Jira tickets — in one place.

useCases.title: Auto-create Todoist tasks from Jira assignments
useCases.description: When a Jira issue is assigned to you, GAIA immediately creates a matching Todoist task with the issue summary, priority, due date, and a direct link to Jira so your personal task list is always current.

useCases.title: Sync Todoist completions back to Jira
useCases.description: When you check off a Jira-linked task in Todoist, GAIA transitions the corresponding Jira issue to your configured Done state so the team board stays accurate without requiring you to open Jira.

useCases.title: Map Jira projects to Todoist projects
useCases.description: GAIA routes Jira assignments to the appropriate Todoist project based on the Jira project key, keeping your engineering work organized separately from personal tasks in your Todoist workspace.

useCases.title: Surface overdue Jira issues as urgent Todoist tasks
useCases.description: When a Jira issue assigned to you passes its due date without being resolved, GAIA creates or updates the Todoist task with urgent priority and an overdue flag so it surfaces prominently in your daily planning.

useCases.title: Daily Jira queue review task in Todoist
useCases.description: Each morning GAIA creates a Todoist task with a summary of your Jira queue — issues in progress, upcoming due dates, and new assignments — so you start the day with a prioritized view of your Jira workload.

howItWorks.step: Connect Jira and Todoist to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Jira account and Todoist account. GAIA identifies your Jira user and maps your assignments to your Todoist workspace.

howItWorks.step: Configure project mapping and completion sync
howItWorks.description: Map Jira project keys to Todoist projects, set the Jira transition that a Todoist completion should trigger, and choose whether GAIA should sync bidirectionally or only from Jira to Todoist.

howItWorks.step: Manage your workload in Todoist with Jira staying current
howItWorks.description: GAIA creates Todoist tasks as you receive Jira assignments and syncs completions back automatically. You plan your day in Todoist while your team sees real-time status in Jira.

faqs.question: Does GAIA create Todoist tasks for all Jira issues in my project or only assignments?
faqs.answer: By default GAIA creates Todoist tasks only for Jira issues assigned to your user. You can optionally extend this to issues you are watching, issues in a specific sprint, or issues with a label you specify.

faqs.question: What Jira transition does GAIA use when I complete a Todoist task?
faqs.answer: During setup you choose which Jira workflow transition maps to Todoist task completion. For most teams this is the Done or Resolved transition, but you can map it to any transition in your project's workflow.

faqs.question: Can I snooze or reschedule a Todoist task without affecting Jira?
faqs.answer: Yes. Rescheduling, snoozing, adding subtasks, or editing the Todoist task title are local-only actions that do not affect Jira. Only task completion triggers a Jira status update.

jira-clickup.tagline: Bridge Jira development tracking with ClickUp product planning seamlessly
jira-clickup.metaTitle: Jira と ClickUp の連携: ストーリーとタスクを双方向同期
jira-clickup.metaDescription: JiraストーリーのステータスをClickUpタスクに同期し、ClickUpからストーリーを作成、優先度やスプリント日程も反映。GAIAが階層を対応付けます。設定手順をご覧ください。
jira-clickup.intro:
Product teams that plan and track delivery in ClickUp often run into a wall when engineering uses Jira for day-to-day development. Each team has legitimate reasons for their tool preference, but the boundary between them creates a coordination overhead that neither team should have to manage manually. Status updates made in Jira do not appear in ClickUp. Requirements changed in ClickUp do not reach engineers in Jira.

GAIA bridges Jira and ClickUp by syncing the relevant data in both directions automatically. Engineering progress in Jira flows to the ClickUp delivery board. Product requirement changes in ClickUp propagate to the corresponding Jira stories. Both teams work in their preferred tool and trust that the other side stays current.

This integration is particularly valuable for organizations that have standardized on ClickUp for company-wide project management but allow engineering to use Jira for its superior development tooling — Agile boards, sprint planning, and deep Atlassian ecosystem integrations.

useCases.title: Sync Jira story status to ClickUp tasks
useCases.description: When a Jira story moves to In Progress or Done, GAIA updates the linked ClickUp task status so product managers always see accurate development progress on their delivery boards without polling engineers.

useCases.title: Create Jira stories from ClickUp feature tasks
useCases.description: When a ClickUp feature task is approved and moved to Ready for Development, GAIA creates a corresponding Jira story with the task description, acceptance criteria, and priority already populated.

useCases.title: Propagate ClickUp priority changes to Jira
useCases.description: When a product manager changes a ClickUp task priority — for example, upgrading a feature from Medium to Critical — GAIA updates the priority of the linked Jira story and notifies the assigned engineer so they can adjust their sprint queue.

useCases.title: Sync Jira sprint dates to ClickUp milestones
useCases.description: GAIA reads Jira sprint start and end dates and creates or updates corresponding ClickUp milestones, keeping the product delivery timeline in ClickUp aligned with actual engineering sprints.

useCases.title: Surface Jira blockers in ClickUp
useCases.description: When a Jira story is marked as blocked, GAIA adds a comment to the linked ClickUp task summarizing the blocker so product managers can take cross-team action without waiting for engineering stand-up.

howItWorks.step: Connect Jira and ClickUp to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Jira project and ClickUp workspace. Map Jira projects to ClickUp Spaces and Folders during initial configuration.

howItWorks.step: Define field mappings and sync direction
howItWorks.description: Map Jira workflow statuses to ClickUp task statuses, define which fields are authoritative in which tool, and configure which events should trigger cross-platform actions.

howItWorks.step: Both tools stay synchronized automatically
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors both platforms for relevant changes and propagates updates in real time. Product managers work in ClickUp; engineers work in Jira; both boards always reflect the same current state.

faqs.question: How does GAIA handle the Jira epic-story-subtask hierarchy versus ClickUp's task-subtask model?
faqs.answer: GAIA maps Jira epics to ClickUp tasks and Jira stories to ClickUp subtasks by default, or you can map each level to a separate ClickUp hierarchy tier. The mapping is configurable to match your team's organizational conventions.

faqs.question: Can GAIA sync Jira custom fields to ClickUp custom fields?
faqs.answer: Yes. During setup you map Jira custom fields to corresponding ClickUp custom fields. GAIA handles type conversion — for example, mapping a Jira number field to a ClickUp numeric field — and logs any fields that cannot be mapped cleanly.

faqs.question: What happens to ClickUp tasks that have no corresponding Jira story?
faqs.answer: GAIA only syncs tasks that match your configured rules — typically tasks that have been explicitly linked or that match a trigger like being moved to a Ready for Development list. Unlinked ClickUp tasks are left untouched.

jira-trello.tagline: Sync Jira bugs to a Trello bug tracker board automatically
jira-trello.metaTitle: Jira と Trello の連携: 両ツールでバグを追跡
jira-trello.metaDescription: JiraとTrelloをGAIAで連携。JiraのバグをTrelloのバグ管理ボードに自動同期し、両ツールの状況を最新に維持。非技術職の関係者もバグの対応状況を把握できます。
jira-trello.intro:
Engineering teams track bugs in Jira because of its tight integration with sprint boards and version management. But non-technical stakeholders — support managers, product owners, customer success leads — often prefer Trello for its visual clarity and accessibility. When bug information lives only in Jira, the stakeholders who need to see it are locked out unless someone manually maintains a parallel Trello board.

GAIA syncs Jira bugs to Trello automatically so stakeholders get the visual bug tracker they prefer while engineering continues working in Jira. New bugs in Jira appear as Trello cards. Status transitions in Jira move Trello cards across lists. When a bug is resolved, the Trello card updates automatically. Nobody has to maintain both boards.

This integration is most valuable for support and customer success teams that need visibility into bug resolution timelines without needing Jira access, and for organizations that want a lightweight external bug visibility board without investing in Jira dashboard configuration.

useCases.title: Mirror Jira bugs to a Trello bug tracker board
useCases.description: When a new bug is created in Jira, GAIA creates a corresponding Trello card with the bug summary, priority, affected version, and a link back to Jira so non-technical stakeholders have a current view of the bug queue.

useCases.title: Move Trello cards when Jira bug status changes
useCases.description: As a Jira bug moves through the workflow — from Open to In Progress to In Review to Resolved — GAIA moves the corresponding Trello card across the matching lists so the Trello board always reflects Jira status in real time.

useCases.title: Add Jira fix version to Trello card labels
useCases.description: When engineering sets a fix version on a Jira bug, GAIA adds the version as a Trello label so stakeholders can filter the bug board by release and understand which fixes are coming in which version.

useCases.title: Post Jira bug comments to Trello card activity
useCases.description: When an engineer adds an investigation update or resolution note to a Jira bug, GAIA mirrors the comment to the Trello card so support staff following the card see the latest engineering notes without Jira access.

useCases.title: Escalate high-priority Jira bugs to a Trello escalation list
useCases.description: When a Jira bug is marked as Critical or Blocker priority, GAIA creates or moves its Trello card to a dedicated Escalations list on the Trello board so critical bugs are visually prominent and easy to track.

howItWorks.step: Connect Jira and Trello to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Jira project and Trello account. Select the Trello board and configure the list structure that should mirror your Jira bug workflow stages.

howItWorks.step: Map Jira statuses to Trello lists
howItWorks.description: Define which Jira workflow statuses correspond to which Trello lists and which Jira issue fields should populate Trello card title, description, labels, and due date.

howItWorks.step: Jira and Trello stay in sync automatically
howItWorks.description: GAIA creates Trello cards for new Jira bugs and moves them as status changes. Engineering works in Jira; stakeholders watch Trello; both views are always accurate.

faqs.question: Does GAIA sync all Jira issue types or only bugs?
faqs.answer: By default GAIA syncs only Jira issues of type Bug. You can extend this to include other issue types such as Tasks or Stories by configuring additional sync rules, each with their own Trello board or list destination.

faqs.question: Can Trello users add comments that sync back to Jira?
faqs.answer: Yes, bidirectional comment sync is supported. When a Trello card member adds a comment, GAIA posts it to the linked Jira issue. You can restrict this to specific Trello board members if you want to limit which comments flow back to Jira.

faqs.question: What happens when a Jira bug is deleted?
faqs.answer: When a Jira bug is deleted, GAIA archives the corresponding Trello card rather than deleting it. This preserves the card history in Trello while keeping the active board clean. You can configure automatic deletion if preferred.

jira-google-calendar.tagline: Add Jira sprint dates and due dates to Google Calendar automatically
jira-google-calendar.metaTitle: Jira + Google Calendar Integration - Sprint Dates in Your Calendar
jira-google-calendar.metaDescription: Connect Jira and Google Calendar with GAIA. Automatically add Jira sprint start and end dates, issue due dates, and release milestones to Google Calendar so engineering deadlines are always visible alongside the rest of your schedule.
jira-google-calendar.intro:
Jira knows when sprints start and end, when issues are due, and when releases are planned. Google Calendar is where engineers and managers live for time management. But sprint dates in Jira do not appear in Google Calendar automatically, meaning engineers have to check two places to understand their upcoming obligations and managers have to manually create calendar events for milestones they can see in Jira.

GAIA connects Jira and Google Calendar so every sprint, due date, and release milestone in Jira appears automatically as a calendar event. Engineers see their engineering deadlines alongside meetings and personal events without switching tools. Managers get calendar reminders for sprint reviews and release dates without manually creating events.

This integration is particularly useful for engineering managers juggling multiple Jira projects who want a single calendar view of all sprint timelines, and for engineers who use Google Calendar as their primary planning tool and want Jira obligations to surface there naturally.

useCases.title: Add Jira sprint start and end dates to Google Calendar
useCases.description: When a new Jira sprint is created, GAIA creates a Google Calendar event spanning the sprint dates with the sprint name, project, and a link to the Jira sprint board so the team sees sprint boundaries in their calendars automatically.

useCases.title: Create calendar events for Jira issue due dates
useCases.description: When a Jira issue assigned to you receives a due date, GAIA creates a Google Calendar reminder event on that date so engineering deadlines appear alongside meetings and personal commitments in a single view.

useCases.title: Add Jira release milestones to the team calendar
useCases.description: When a Jira version is created with a release date, GAIA adds a milestone event to the shared engineering Google Calendar so the entire team sees upcoming release dates without checking the Jira releases page.

useCases.title: Update calendar events when Jira dates change
useCases.description: When a Jira sprint is extended or an issue due date is pushed, GAIA updates the corresponding Google Calendar event automatically so calendar dates always reflect the current Jira schedule without manual corrections.

useCases.title: Schedule sprint ceremonies from Jira sprint dates
useCases.description: When a Jira sprint is created, GAIA schedules recurring Google Calendar invites for sprint planning, daily standup, sprint review, and retrospective based on the sprint dates and the team's configured ceremony schedule.

howItWorks.step: Connect Jira and Google Calendar to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Jira account and Google Workspace. Select which Jira projects and calendars should be synchronized and which team members should be invited to calendar events.

howItWorks.step: Configure which Jira events create calendar entries
howItWorks.description: Choose whether GAIA should sync sprint dates, issue due dates, release milestones, or all three. Set the calendar destination for each event type and configure reminder timing.

howItWorks.step: Jira deadlines appear in Google Calendar automatically
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors Jira for sprint creation, date changes, and release updates and keeps Google Calendar current. Engineers see engineering obligations in their calendar without any manual event creation.

faqs.question: Does GAIA create individual calendar events for every Jira issue due date or only sprints?
faqs.answer: Both are configurable. You can sync sprint dates only, issue due dates only, or both. For issue due dates, you can filter by assignee so only issues assigned to each team member create events on their personal calendar.

faqs.question: What happens to Google Calendar events when a Jira sprint is deleted?
faqs.answer: GAIA deletes or cancels the corresponding Google Calendar event when a Jira sprint is deleted. If the sprint is renamed or its dates are changed, GAIA updates the calendar event to match.

faqs.question: Can GAIA add Jira issue due date reminders to a shared team calendar?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can configure GAIA to write to a shared Google Calendar that all team members subscribe to. This gives the team a unified view of all upcoming Jira deadlines without each member needing personal calendar sync enabled.

jira-figma.tagline: Link Figma designs to Jira tickets and streamline design review workflows
jira-figma.metaTitle: Figma と Jira の連携: デザインをチケットに添付
jira-figma.metaDescription: FigmaとJiraの連携はFigma for Jiraアプリで課題にデザインを表示。GAIAはJira側を担当し、デザインリンク付きの課題作成やデザイナーへの通知を行います。
jira-figma.intro:
FigmaとJiraを連携するには、Atlassian MarketplaceからFigma for Jiraアプリをインストールします。FigmaのファイルやフレームのリンクをJiraの課題に貼り付けると、課題内にデザインのライブプレビューが表示されます。Figma側では、Dev Mode向けのJiraプラグインやFigJam向けのJiraウィジェットで、ファイルの中から課題を表示したりリンクしたりできます。この2つで、JiraへのFigmaの埋め込みと、デザインとチケットのリンクはカバーできます。

GAIAはFigmaには接続しないため、ファイル内のフレーム、バージョン、コメントは読み取れません。GAIAが担うのは、デザインの受け渡しに伴うJira側の作業です。渡されたFigmaのリンクを入れて課題を作成し、ワークフローに沿ってステータスを進め、コメントし、対応が必要なときにはSlackやメールでデザイナーやエンジニアに知らせます。

GAIAにはJiraのイベントトリガーがないため、これらの定型作業は設定したスケジュール（1時間ごと、毎朝など）か、頼んだときに実行されます。Figmaでの変更を即座にJiraへ反映したい場合は、GAIAではなくFigma for JiraアプリやFigmaのプラグインを使ってください。

useCases.title: デザインのリンク付きでJiraの課題を作成
useCases.description: チャットにFigmaのリンクを貼って作業内容を説明すると、GAIAが適切なプロジェクトに要約、説明、FigmaのURLを入れたJiraの課題を作成します。Figma for Jiraアプリがプレビューを表示できます。

useCases.title: デザインレビューのメモをJiraの課題に変換
useCases.description: レビューのメモや修正依頼の一覧を貼り付けると、GAIAが項目ごとに関連するFigmaのリンク付きでJiraの課題を作成し、指定した担当者とラベルも設定します。

useCases.title: チケットが開発に入ったことをデザイナーに通知
useCases.description: スケジュールに沿って、GAIAは前回の実行以降に進行中になったデザインラベル付きの課題をJiraで探し、課題のリンクをSlackやメールでデザイナーに送ります。

useCases.title: デザイン受け渡しの週次レポートを送信
useCases.description: 毎週、GAIAがJiraでデザイン関連の課題を検索し、デザイン待ちのもの、開発中のもの、説明にFigmaのリンクがない課題をまとめて送ります。

useCases.title: デザインに関連するJiraの課題を探す
useCases.description: あるFigmaファイルに触れているJiraの課題はどれかと尋ねると、GAIAが課題の本文からリンクやファイル名を検索し、ステータスと担当者付きで一覧にします。

howItWorks.step: Figma for Jiraをインストールし、JiraをGAIAに接続
howItWorks.description: デザインのプレビュー用に、Jira CloudのサイトにFigma for Jiraアプリをインストールします。次に、GAIAの連携ページからAtlassianアカウントでJiraを接続します。通知を送らせたい場合はSlackやGmailも接続してください。

howItWorks.step: 定型作業を普段の言葉で説明
howItWorks.description: ワークフローを作成します。たとえば「平日の毎朝10時に、APPプロジェクトでdesignラベルが付き、昨日進行中になった課題を探して、#designでデザイナーに知らせて」です。チャットでFigmaのリンクから課題を作るよう頼むこともできます。

howItWorks.step: GAIAがバックグラウンドで実行
howItWorks.description: スケジュールのワークフローは設定どおりに実行され、何をしたかを報告します。課題やコメントの削除など取り消しにくい操作は、承認設定に従って事前に確認を求めます。

faqs.question: GAIAはどのFigmaフレームがどのJiraチケットに対応するかをどう判断しますか？
faqs.answer: GAIAはFigmaのファイルを開けないため、フレーム名で照合することはありません。渡されたFigmaのURLで課題とデザインを結びつけ、特定のFigmaリンクやファイル名を含む課題をJiraで検索できます。

faqs.question: GAIAはJiraのチケットにFigmaのプレビューを埋め込めますか？
faqs.answer: プレビューを表示するのはGAIAではなくFigma for Jiraアプリです。GAIAが課題にFigmaのURLを入れ、アプリがインストールされていればJiraがデザインのプレビューを表示します。

faqs.question: GAIAはFigmaのブランチを使ったワークフローに対応していますか？
faqs.answer: GAIAはFigmaを読み取らないため、ブランチやマージは見えません。ブランチのリンクを渡せば課題にそのリンクを使い、マージ後にはメインファイルのリンクに差し替えるよう頼めます。

faqs.question: JiraにFigmaを追加するには？
faqs.answer: Atlassian MarketplaceからFigma for Jiraアプリをインストールし（Jiraの管理者の承認が必要な場合があります）、アプリの案内に従ってFigmaアカウントを接続します。あとはFigmaのファイルやフレームのリンクを課題に貼ると、デザインが表示されます。

faqs.question: Figma用のJiraプラグインはありますか？
faqs.answer: はい。Figmaのプラグインとウィジェットの一覧に、Dev Mode向けのJiraプラグインとFigJam向けのJiraウィジェットがあり、ファイル内でJiraの課題を表示してリンクできます。一覧でJiraを検索してください。GAIAが担当するのはJira側だけです。

faqs.question: GAIAでJiraのチケットとFigmaを同期できますか？
faqs.answer: 直接はできません。GAIAはFigmaに接続しないため、デザインの変更を検知できません。GAIAはJira側（リンク、ステータス、コメント、通知）をスケジュールで整え、課題内のデザインのプレビューはFigma for Jiraアプリが最新に保ちます。

jira-discord.tagline: Post Jira issue updates to Discord dev channels automatically
jira-discord.metaTitle: Jira + Discord Integration - Engineering Updates in Your Dev Server
jira-discord.metaDescription: Connect Jira and Discord with GAIA. Automatically post Jira ticket updates, sprint summaries, and blocker alerts to your Discord engineering channels so the team stays informed without monitoring Jira.
jira-discord.intro:
Engineering teams that use Discord as their primary communication hub often find that Jira activity stays invisible in their day-to-day chat. A critical bug is created in Jira but nobody in Discord knows until the next standup. A sprint closes with impressive velocity but the team never sees a summary. Engineers have to tab over to Jira just to find out if their PR review is unblocking the issue they care about.

GAIA brings Jira into Discord by routing the right events to the right channels automatically. Sprint summaries land in the engineering channel at the end of every sprint. Critical bugs trigger immediate alerts. Assigned issues notify engineers in DMs. Teams can also create and update Jira tickets with Discord commands without leaving their chat environment.

This integration is most impactful for remote engineering teams who run Discord as their virtual office and want Jira activity to flow into their existing communication rhythm rather than requiring constant tool switching.

useCases.title: Post sprint summaries to the engineering channel
useCases.description: When a Jira sprint closes, GAIA posts a formatted summary to the designated Discord channel including stories completed, velocity, carry-over issues, and top contributors so the team celebrates progress and understands what carried forward.

useCases.title: Alert the team to new critical bugs
useCases.description: When a Jira issue of type Bug is created or upgraded to Critical priority, GAIA immediately posts an alert to the engineering Discord channel with the bug title, reporter, affected component, and link so the team can respond quickly.

useCases.title: DM engineers when Jira issues are assigned
useCases.description: When a Jira issue is assigned to an engineer, GAIA sends them a Discord DM with the issue summary, priority, sprint, and a direct Jira link so they are notified in the tool they are already using.

useCases.title: Post blocker notifications to the leads channel
useCases.description: When a Jira story transitions to Blocked, GAIA posts a structured notification to the team leads Discord channel identifying the blocking dependency and the affected engineer so resolution can be coordinated immediately.

useCases.title: Create Jira tickets from Discord slash commands
useCases.description: Engineers can type a GAIA slash command in Discord to create a new Jira ticket without leaving the chat. GAIA collects the issue type, summary, and priority through a short Discord prompt and creates the ticket, posting the confirmation back to the channel.

howItWorks.step: Connect Jira and Discord to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Jira project and invite the GAIA bot to your Discord server. Map Jira projects and issue types to Discord channels during setup.

howItWorks.step: Configure event routing and notification format
howItWorks.description: Choose which Jira events generate Discord messages, which channels or users should receive each event type, and the format of notification embeds.

howItWorks.step: Jira activity flows into Discord in real time
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors Jira and posts updates to the configured Discord destinations as they happen. The team stays informed without leaving Discord.

faqs.question: Can GAIA route Jira notifications from different projects to different Discord channels?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can configure separate channel routing rules for each Jira project. For example, mobile Jira tickets go to #mobile-dev and backend tickets go to #backend-dev. You can also route by issue type or priority regardless of project.

faqs.question: How does GAIA match Discord users to Jira users for DM notifications?
faqs.answer: During setup you provide a mapping of Jira usernames to Discord user IDs. GAIA uses this mapping to send direct messages to the correct Discord user when their Jira account receives an assignment.

faqs.question: Can GAIA avoid posting every minor Jira event and keep Discord signal quality high?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA's event filter configuration is very granular. Most teams set it to notify only on issue creation, status transitions to specific states, priority escalations, and sprint boundaries. Routine field edits and comment additions are excluded by default.

jira-drive.tagline: Attach requirement docs from Google Drive to Jira epics automatically
jira-drive.metaTitle: Jira と Google Drive の連携: 要件をエピックに紐付け
jira-drive.metaDescription: JiraとGoogle DriveをGAIAで連携。Driveの要件ドキュメントをJiraのエピックに自動添付し、解決した障害から事後分析の文書を作成。開発文書を進行中の作業と結び付けます。
jira-drive.intro:
Every Jira epic has documentation that lives somewhere in Google Drive: the product requirements document, the technical design doc, the stakeholder sign-off email, the post-launch notes. But finding and attaching those documents to the right Jira epic is manual work that often does not happen, leaving engineers to dig through Drive each time they need context.

GAIA builds and maintains the link between Google Drive documents and Jira epics automatically. When a product requirements document is created in Drive with a matching name, GAIA attaches it to the corresponding Jira epic. When an incident is resolved in Jira, GAIA creates a post-mortem document in Drive. The documentation system and the issue tracking system stay connected without anyone manually managing the relationship.

This integration reduces the context-gathering overhead that slows engineers down at the start of each task and ensures that the rationale behind engineering decisions is always accessible from the Jira issue where the work is tracked.

useCases.title: Auto-attach Drive requirement docs to Jira epics
useCases.description: When a new Google Doc is added to the requirements folder in Drive with a name matching a Jira epic, GAIA attaches the document link to the epic so engineers immediately have access to the full specification without searching Drive.

useCases.title: Create Jira epics from new Drive PRDs
useCases.description: When a Product Requirements Document is created in Drive and marked as Ready for Engineering, GAIA creates a Jira epic with the PRD title, a summary of the requirements, and a link back to the Drive document so engineering can begin planning immediately.

useCases.title: Generate post-mortem documents from resolved Jira incidents
useCases.description: When a Jira incident issue is transitioned to Resolved, GAIA creates a post-mortem document in Drive pre-populated with the incident title, timeline from Jira comments, and a structured template so the team can complete the analysis without starting from a blank page.

useCases.title: Attach technical design docs to Jira stories
useCases.description: When an engineer creates a technical design document in Drive and includes a Jira story key in the document title, GAIA attaches the document to the referenced Jira story so future engineers can find the design rationale in the issue.

useCases.title: Maintain a Drive folder structure mirroring Jira projects
useCases.description: GAIA creates and maintains a Google Drive folder structure that mirrors your Jira project hierarchy. When a new Jira project or epic is created, GAIA creates the corresponding Drive folder so document organization stays consistent automatically.

howItWorks.step: Connect Google Drive and Jira to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Google Workspace account and Jira project. Designate the Drive folders GAIA should monitor and map them to Jira projects.

howItWorks.step: Configure naming conventions and trigger rules
howItWorks.description: Define the naming patterns GAIA should use to match Drive documents to Jira epics and stories, which Drive events should create Jira issues, and which Jira events should create Drive documents.

howItWorks.step: Docs attach to Jira issues automatically
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors both platforms and maintains links between documents and issues in real time. Engineers click through from Jira to the right Drive document without searching; documents in Drive reference their linked Jira issues.

faqs.question: Does GAIA require documents to follow a specific naming format?
faqs.answer: GAIA works best with consistent naming but supports flexible matching patterns including partial name matches and regular expressions. You can also link Drive documents to Jira epics manually and GAIA will maintain those explicit links going forward.

faqs.question: Can GAIA attach files from shared drives, not just personal Drive?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA can access any Google Drive location that the authorized Google account has access to, including shared drives and files shared with the domain. It respects existing Drive sharing permissions and does not modify them.

faqs.question: What happens to Drive links in Jira when a document is moved to a different Drive folder?
faqs.answer: Google Drive URLs are stable and do not change when a file is moved between folders. Jira links remain valid after file moves. GAIA does log the move event so you have a record of where the document currently lives.

jira-hubspot.tagline: Sync customer bug reports from HubSpot to Jira tickets automatically
jira-hubspot.metaTitle: Jira と HubSpot の連携: 顧客のバグを素早く開発へ
jira-hubspot.metaDescription: JiraとHubSpotをGAIAで連携。HubSpotの顧客からのバグ報告をJiraのチケットに自動作成し、商談の背景を課題に添付。解決時には担当者に通知し、素早く対応できます。
jira-hubspot.intro:
Customer-reported bugs logged in HubSpot need to reach engineering in Jira, but the handoff is almost always manual.
